extDescription.message: Blocks ads, collects hidden ones into a tray, and warns you about fake web addresses. Open source, no data collection.

aggressiveHint.message: Also hides boxes that look like ads (ad-slot IDs, “Advertisement” labels). It may hide something by mistake: if so, untick “on this site”.

w_intro.message: An ad blocker that shows you what it hid, and warns you when a web address is pretending to be another site. Everything runs on your device.

w_step_pin.message: Pin the GoGoChay icon to the toolbar (puzzle-piece menu → pin), so the tray is one click away.

w_step_perm.message: Safari, Firefox and phones: allow GoGoChay on all websites (Safari: Settings › Extensions › "Always Allow on Every Website"; Firefox: about:addons › GoGoChay › Permissions). Without it, ads are blocked but ad boxes stay visible.

w_step_tray.message: On any page, click the icon to open the tray: see what was hidden, hide more, or pause GoGoChay for that site.

w_ads_1.message: Blocks ad requests with EasyList, Liste FR (French sites) and ABPVN (Vietnamese sites). The browser does the blocking, so GoGoChay never sees your traffic.

w_ads_2.message: Hides banners, “Sponsored” blocks and empty ad placeholders as the page loads.

w_ads_3.message: Aggressive blocking (off by default) also hides boxes that look like ads on sites no list covers, e.g. empty boxes labelled “Advertisement”. Can be turned off per site.

w_tray_1.message: Lists every ad hidden on the page: where it comes from, its size, its text.

w_tray_2.message: Show an ad again (or all of them) if hiding it broke the page.

w_tray_3.message: “Hide an element…”: click or tap anything the lists missed. It stays hidden on that site; “Undo” removes it.

w_tray_4.message: Pause GoGoChay on a site, switch the language, open it in the side panel (Chrome) or sidebar (Firefox).

w_fake_intro.message: GoGoChay checks the address of the page you actually land on, even after a redirect from Facebook, an e-mail or a chat, and warns you if it is made to look like another site.

w_fake_red.message: The name mixes alphabets, uses rare letters that only look like a–z, or imitates a well-known site (banks, PayPal, Google, Ameli, Vietcombank…).

w_fake_yellow_t.message: 🟡 Yellow note: check before you log in

w_fake_yellow.message: The name has characters outside a–z (often harmless accents). GoGoChay only reminds you when you click into a password or card-number field.

w_fake_note.message: The warning highlights the fake letters and tells you the name of the site you are actually on, with “Leave this site” and “I know this site” buttons. It catches lookalike names; for brand-new scam sites, keep your browser’s own phishing protection on.

w_priv_1.message: No data leaves your device: no network requests, no analytics, no remote updates.

w_priv_2.message: Only your own settings are stored, locally: paused sites, elements you hid, language, trusted sites.

w_priv_3.message: Open source (MIT). The filter lists are rebuilt from public sources in CI and can be checked by anyone.

langCode.description: Do not translate: language code of this file

spoofDisclaimer.message: Automatic warning based on suspicious characters in the address. It may be wrong: it does not prove the site is fraudulent, and no warning does not mean a site is safe.

w_disclaimer.message: Warnings are automatic: they look only at the characters of the address and its resemblance to well-known names, not at the page itself. They can be wrong in both directions: a warning does not prove a site is fraudulent, and no warning does not mean a site is safe. Brand names are used only for comparison; GoGoChay is not affiliated with them.

w_tagline.message: Ads tucked away. Fakes called out.
